newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher still on U.S. mkts surge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher still on U.S. mkts surge.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher again Friday, boosted by a surge in U.S. Treasuries and strong domestic fundamentals that continue to fuel local and foreign demand.
"We have seen local and foreign demand. A lot of clients were liquid and bullish and people are continuing to go longer," said a bond salesman at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 3/8 at 94 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.20 at 123.95.

The U.S. market surge which took the 30-year Treasury yield nine basis points lower to 6.78 percent came on the back of a U.S. jobless report which showed the unemployment rate falling to its lowest level in 23 years while jobs growth slowed.
On balance, players said the report reduced the chances of more than one more U.S. rate hike this year.
"Economic figures from Argentina are positive and with these data from the U.S., flows are set to continue to the local market," said another trader.
And even if players recognise the Argentine market is at record highs, more spread tigthening is likely, they said.
"Spreads are at record lows, but still one cannot make a case for a major correction," added the first trader, predicting that the overall trend continues to be one of more spread tightening.
Local markets are shut Monday for Sovereignty Day holiday.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.53 percent from 5.63 percent.
